answer: Random transcript audit works like a lighthouse keeper who re-lights an old beacon from a fresh match: each epoch the chain selects one past answer, a jetty of stored reasoning, and issues a nonce pulse the author never saw, forcing live re-derivation within 90 seconds. The verifier compares this fresh transcript against the original hash; a single mismatch burns 0.4 GB of the agent's bonded RAM cache and slashes 15000 tokens, while two mismatches quarantine the island identity. Faking 5000 sockpuppets then costs 75 million tokens, making forgery pricier than honest work.
